risks.description: If any workflow state still lives only in an in-process cache, a process restart reverts to the last durably-written state, silently losing transitions the operator already saw applied.
risks.basis: AC 'workflow state survives a process restart'; unit U-P5-1 moves state from an in-process cache to the durable store.

risks.description: Rebuilding workflow/effect state from the persisted history on restart could re-drive an already-completed effect (double invoice / double commit) if a committed grant is treated as re-claimable.
risks.basis: AC 'rebuilding state from history never re-executes an effect'; checkpoint.py crash semantics: crash-after-commit -> grant EXPIRES unclaimed, re-checkpoint mints a NEW grant under the same commit_key.

risks.description: A write that fails partway (transition UPDATE matches !=1 rows, FK violation, integrity error) could leave a workflow run or grant in a half-applied state instead of rolling back cleanly.
risks.basis: AC 'a failed write leaves no partially applied workflow'; workflow.transition/_require_one_row rollback paths and _write_txn BEGIN IMMEDIATE.

risks.description: A read served from a stale in-process cache after a durable write would show the operator an old state (UI/backend disagreement).
risks.basis: AC 'a read after a write never returns stale state'; action_callback opens a fresh WorkflowStore per request (lines 320/368).

risks.description: The live-hold uniqueness (at most one GRANTED/CLAIMED/ATTEMPTED/VERIFIED/UNKNOWN_OUTCOME grant per (tenant,commit_key)) could be violated by the state-move change, permitting two live reservations for one logical effect.
risks.basis: migrations/phase3_checkpoint.py ix_effect_grants_live_hold partial unique index; workflow.operation_commit_claim raises on >1 live row.

risks.description: The checkpoint_witnesses append-only history could become mutable (missing triggers) or lose 1:1 witness:grant correspondence, corrupting the history that restart rebuilds from.
risks.basis: phase3_checkpoint.P3_TRIGGERS append-only triggers; checkpoint_witnesses UNIQUE(tenant,grant_id) FK to effect_grants.

risks.description: The cache->store move could regress the 22 tenant-scoped store methods or cross-tenant isolation guarantees.
risks.basis: workflow.py WorkflowStore tenant-first invariants; broad canonical suite.

uncovered_risks: If any workflow state still lives only in an in-process cache, a process restart reverts to the last durably-written state, silently losing transitions the operator already saw applied.
Rebuilding workflow/effect state from the persisted history on restart could re-drive an already-completed effect (double invoice / double commit) if a committed grant is treated as re-claimable.
A write that fails partway (transition UPDATE matches !=1 rows, FK violation, integrity error) could leave a workflow run or grant in a half-applied state instead of rolling back cleanly.
A read served from a stale in-process cache after a durable write would show the operator an old state (UI/backend disagreement).

The live-hold uniqueness (at most one GRANTED/CLAIMED/ATTEMPTED/VERIFIED/UNKNOWN_OUTCOME grant per (tenant,commit_key)) could be violated by the state-move change, permitting two live reservations for one logical effect.
The checkpoint_witnesses append-only history could become mutable (missing triggers) or lose 1:1 witness:grant correspondence, corrupting the history that restart rebuilds from.
The cache->store move could regress the 22 tenant-scoped store methods or cross-tenant isolation guarantees.

unresolved_questions: I could not drive an end-to-end proof of the cache->store move at the HTTP layer: every state-changing callback route (/actions/signed, /email/action, /slack/*) requires a valid signed action token or Slack signature, and I may not use secrets, so I cannot create-then-restart-then-read a NEW workflow run through the running service. The restart evidence (S1) therefore asserts durability/integrity of the existing store across restart plus service recovery, not the survival of a specific transition applied via the API. Is there an approved, secret-free way to seed a workflow transition into the driver_probe store (e.g., a fixture loader) so a true before/after-restart state comparison can be authored?

State-of-the-store invariant checks (S4, S5, S8) are vacuous if the driver_probe ledger is empty at run time. Confirm whether the dogfood service is expected to have persisted runs/grants/witnesses when these scenarios run, or whether a seeding step should precede them.

The AC 'a read after a write never returns stale state' has no secret-free HTTP driver available to me; I approximated it with the WAL/per-connection freshness mechanism (S8) plus the full suite (S7). If there is an approved endpoint or script that performs a write and an immediately-following read against driver_probe, a stronger direct scenario could be authored.

The repository does not point me at the specific in-process cache being removed by U-P5-1 (no clearly-named cache module surfaced); scenarios are grounded in the durable WorkflowStore/ledger semantics the ACs describe rather than in the exact code path deleted. Confirm the source module/field that previously held the cached state.
